items.text: Incoming-wave intel opens readable details on tap or keyboard, including on phones. Base Biomass and enemy stats are clearly labeled, and elite counts explain how many are included in the wave.
Run Build now includes expandable Run conditions: review your doctrine, sworn vows, active Threat modifiers, biome and current event on phone or desktop.

Manual backups now report when a snapshot could not be saved and offer Export JSON as a fallback. Failed backup writes preserve older snapshots, and corrupt current-save data is no longer copied into the backup list.

Restoring a backup now asks for confirmation and keeps a recovery snapshot of readable current progress. Failed storage writes no longer claim success, and the selected backup stays available for retry even when the backup list is full.

Choosing a save file now opens a review showing its name, currency, best wave and run count. Nothing is imported until you choose Replace progress; Cancel or Escape keeps your current progress, and invalid or unreadable files show a clear error.

Confirmed save imports now finish their storage writes before replacing the active session. If the recovery backup or imported save cannot be written, current progress stays intact; a competing browser tab also blocks the import until you reload.

Backup restoration now respects browser-tab ownership and keeps the latest live progress in its recovery snapshot, including changes waiting to be saved. A successful restore also clears the old pending save so it cannot run afterward.

The Memory Archive now lets you search revealed titles, bonuses and unlock hints, and filter recovered or unrecovered memories. Locked story details stay hidden, replay buttons are easier to tap, and the archive explains that recovered bonuses already apply automatically.

Collection rank-up celebrations now support keyboard focus, Escape dismissal and live reduced-motion preferences. Long promotion lists scroll within the popup, keeping Continue reachable on small screens and in landscape.

Collection browsing now keeps keyboard focus with you: arrow keys, Home and End switch Codex sections, opening a category focuses its heading, and returning to all categories restores the tile you came from.

Undiscovered collection entries now use a clear, readable label instead of dim question marks. Tooltips keep unrevealed names hidden, while discovered entries retain their names, status and mastery counts.
The optional debug music console now gives its boss-name field and sliders larger touch targets, including on tablets.

Story cutscenes now respond to motion and flash settings while playing. Reduced motion keeps a still image, restoring motion preserves the scene clock without replaying elapsed sound cues, and the ending card keeps its dimmed backdrop in either mode.

The opening cinematic now follows motion and flash preferences live, from its start screen through the film. Restoring animation skips elapsed sound cues, and requesting reduced motion during the final dive exits cleanly without getting stuck.

Story cutscenes now preserve scene and ending-card reading time while their tab is hidden. Captions and scene animation pause, and returning continues the same visual timeline without a backlog of sound cues.

The opening cinematic now pauses its start-screen animation, scene reading time, captions, and final dive while its tab is hidden. Returning resumes from the same point, with no skipped scenes or overdue sound burst.

Update briefings now keep keyboard focus inside the dialog, return focus when dismissed, and support Escape. Release highlights and changes can be focused and scrolled with the keyboard, while new-player and mechanic-introduction priorities stay unchanged.

New-system introductions now keep keyboard focus inside each card and move it to the next queued introduction. Escape acknowledges the current card or batch, scrolling lists are keyboard-accessible, and closing the queue restores the original control.

Selecting a Field Manual topic now brings its article into focus, including on narrow screens. Press Enter from search to read the selected result, and use Back to topics to return to its index entry without losing your search.

Tutorial and field-guide text now follows live motion preferences, including Allow motion. Reduced motion reveals the whole sentence immediately, restoring motion does not hide text already read, and assistive technology receives the complete sentence throughout the visual reveal.

Finishing a field guide with the keyboard now focuses Stay here and makes the completion result available from its controls. Escape closes the completion card, buttons fit narrow screens with larger touch targets, and a separate ceremony opened by your action keeps its focus.

Profile Power explanations expand with a tap, Enter, or Space and stay open while you read. The rows have larger interaction targets, and multiplier values show more precision so small positive bonuses are not rounded away.

Career statistics with explanations now have keyboard- and touch-accessible Details controls. Explanations stay open inline while you read, including after reopening their section, and ordinary statistic cards stay compact.

Global standings now offer Retry after an unavailable response and Refresh after loading, with announced status and labeled table columns. Changing boards clears old results while loading, and delayed responses cannot replace the current board.

Replay sharing now shows a selectable link or code when clipboard access is denied or unavailable. Preparing/copy feedback is localized, duplicate requests are disabled while pending, and results from an older replay cannot overwrite the current control.

Replay Theater now keeps keyboard focus inside the viewer, restores the opener on exit, and focuses the outcome action when playback finishes. Pause/speed/progress expose their state, and Skip to outcome works even while paused.
Skipping a replay to its outcome no longer compresses skipped combat sounds into a sudden burst. Normal playback, including faster playback speeds, keeps its combat audio.

The Replay Theater paste field accepts copied replay links as well as raw codes, supports Enter to watch, and shows localized checking/error feedback. Editing the input or leaving the screen prevents an older decode from opening the wrong replay.
Update briefing links and the Never show again control now have larger touch targets, making release information easier to use on tablets.

Account level-up notices stay visible while hovered or keyboard-focused and include a keyboard-accessible dismiss button. Focus follows queued notices and returns afterward; a notice resumed after an unlock announcement no longer repeats its sound.

Dismissing reward cards with the keyboard now moves focus to the next card, or back to the previous page control when the stack is cleared. Dismiss All and a disappearing stack footer follow the same rule without stealing unrelated focus.

Bio-Container notices stay readable while hovered or keyboard-focused, with a dismiss button that follows queued rewards and returns focus afterward. Dismissing a notice with Space does not start a wave.

Update-ready prompts wait until you return to the hub, keeping refresh controls out of active runs, tutorials, and Arena matches. Updates downloaded before the prompt mounts are still detected, and dismissing the notice restores keyboard focus.

Achievement cards show Earned, In progress, or Undiscovered in text, with brighter unfinished goals and clearly named Genome Core rewards. Ladder cards also preview their next reward; secret milestones remain concealed until earned.

The Trophy Rack labels mounted and owned organs, explains full-rack restrictions and locked trophy sources, and shows when the next slot unlocks. Mounted trophies expose their selected state to assistive technology, while unavailable trophy details remain readable.

Find achievement milestones faster with name/description search and All, Not earned, and Earned filters. A live result count and clear empty state help you narrow the list; hidden milestone names stay unsearchable until earned.
Screen readers now identify the selected game speed. Call early names the next wave, its overlap and Biomass reward; Splice explains its live Biomass cost and extra Gene Card choice.
The Hero Ops ability wheel now follows your actual cooldown after upgrades and modifiers. Its tooltip and screen-reader description distinguish recovering, recharging, ready and armed abilities.
Selected heroes now show their effective ability and skill cooldowns after upgrades. Downed heroes display unavailable cooldowns instead of suggesting their abilities are ready.

Hero attack and pulse gauges now follow the interval actually used in combat, including haste and siege heroes switching between normal attacks and mega-boss raids. The attack-speed readout matches that cadence.
Hero recovery countdowns now account for faster-revival symbiotes, keeping the battlefield label, HUD and hero panels consistent with the actual time remaining.
Buying a cooldown upgrade during recharge no longer makes the ability gauge jump backward. The active gauge follows its current cast; the shorter cooldown is shown when it is ready for the next cast.

Tap or keyboard-activate the Hero Ops ability wheel to read its status and description inside the panel. The explanation stays readable instead of being clipped at the panel edge; Escape closes it without interrupting play.

Conveyor recycling now shows the correct zero refund for the free starting organism. Recycling or merging a card keeps keyboard focus on a remaining placement option, and merge/recycle buttons identify their organism and cost or refund.
Recycling a conveyor organism now plays one confirmation sound instead of two overlapping copies. Unsuccessful attempts remain silent.

Tower sale and first-branch confirmations now open with Cancel focused, contain keyboard navigation, and close with Escape. Pausing cancels an unfinished confirmation, keeping the Pause controls visible and focused.
After a tower upgrade, keyboard focus stays useful even when the path is complete or the next tier is unaffordable: it moves to the selected tier preview instead of disappearing from the controls.
Tower confirmations keep up with Hive Intelligence: sell refunds update as the tower improves, and an outdated upgrade confirmation cannot purchase an unintended, more expensive tier.

Sound-effect volume and mute changes fade smoothly over a brief instant, avoiding abrupt cuts during playback. Rapid slider changes follow your latest setting, and adjusting the level while muted keeps the game quiet.
The music slider now takes priority over an earlier automatic fade. Turning music down to zero stays silent instead of having an old recovery fade bring the volume back up.
Turning music back on restores the current scene's soundtrack immediately, including its boss theme. Scene changes made while muted are remembered, without replaying old victory or defeat music.
Music off now smoothly silences the entire soundtrack, including musical reward flourishes already playing. Changes in battle pressure or volume cannot bring music back while it is muted.

Screen readers can now identify armed tower and conveyor placements and whether hero auto-cast is on. Conveyor deploy buttons name the organism and its cost; auto-cast keeps its purchase behavior until unlocked.

Reduced motion keeps hero upgrade results visible instead of fading them away instantly. Rapid purchases show the latest gain clearly, and Power and Mastery notices stay still under both device and in-game motion settings.

Hero symbiote previews pause when off-screen or the page is hidden, and respond immediately to motion-preference changes. Tower previews now follow the in-game motion override too. Reduced-motion hero portraits retain their artwork without spinning decorations.

Tower star celebrations now support keyboard dismissal and restore focus. Cosmetic unlock ceremonies now focus their main action, keep keyboard navigation inside the card, and carry focus forward through multiple unlocks. Escape skips the ceremony and returns you to the previous control; unlocked items remain in the Specimen Cabinet.

Genetic Vault openings can be followed by keyboard from hatching through card flips, highlights and harvest. Focus stays with the active reveal, including replay highlights, and returns when you close it. The harvest focuses Collect or Return so hatching another container stays a deliberate choice. Heartbeat motion responds to live motion settings, and flash and shake effects respect their settings.

Reward notifications and Vault Power totals expose the final amount to screen readers while the visible numbers count up. Merged rewards update that amount without announcing every animation frame. Notifications stay available while you hover, focus a control or read an expanded summary; incoming rewards keep your active card in view.
Choosing the screen or hub you are already viewing now closes the phone navigation drawer, without adding an extra Back step.

Progress bars now expose accurate fractional values to screen readers instead of rounding partial unlocks to complete. Conveyor growth bars identify the organism and report progress and time remaining.

Gene drafting respects keyboard focus: Enter activates the selected card, Stop Hive Intelligence, or reroll without accidentally taking the recommended gene. Paused drafts ignore card picks, and typing in a text field no longer triggers draft shortcuts.

Pause-menu settings and confirmation buttons now work correctly with Enter and Space. Resuming with Space no longer also starts a wave, and board shortcuts stay quiet while paused, inside the hero console, or typing in a text field. Pause-menu focus stays inside its controls, returns when closed, and starts on Keep Playing when confirming abandonment. On phones, the pause menu stays above open run drawers so Resume remains reachable.

Evolution purchases now work with Enter and Space as well as clicking or holding. Hero upgrade buttons name the upgrade and Biomass cost, keep keyboard focus after buying, and show the correct level after buying several upgrades. The hero console stays above game-speed controls so its Close button remains clickable.

Switching champions in the Hero Combat Console now shows recovery, shield, and actual ability countdown for the selected hero. Heroes without a basic attack no longer display an infinite attack rate. Use arrow keys, Home, and End to move between roster tabs.
Hero upgrades give immediate purchase feedback while the console is paused, without replaying those sounds when you resume. Conveyor strain purchases also avoid duplicate sound feedback.

Field notes stay visible while you hover over or focus them, giving you time to read. A keyboard-accessible Dismiss button replaces the tap-only hint; notes still clear automatically during normal play and when a gene draft opens.
Inspecting a reward category no longer advances the reveal sequence. Post-run choices now support arrow keys, Home and End, with one Tab stop for the group.
Reward sounds wait while a milestone cinematic covers the results, then resume once without repeating cues already heard.

Field Manual search includes advice, locations and common mistakes, accepts punctuation differences, and finds words across sections. New searches select their best match; related topics open correctly and receive keyboard focus.
Tower portraits rest when scrolled out of view or when the tab is hidden. Device reduced-motion changes immediately switch them to a complete still; returning to the portrait resumes its animation.

Wallet totals now roll smoothly from the number currently shown when rewards or spending overlap, instead of jumping to an unfinished animation’s target. Reduced-motion updates clear the gain highlight correctly.
Currency explanations now receive keyboard focus when opened. Escape returns to the chip, Tab moves naturally onward, and screen readers can identify the chip’s popup.
Reward toasts and vault totals now honor device reduced motion directly, including changes made during a count-up. Re-enabling motion leaves completed totals intact.
Hero portraits now use the same class symbols as the rest of the game, including Resonant’s proper diamond-within-diamond mark.

Opening and story films now offer Read at my pace: reveal all scene text and choose when to advance. Keyboard players can use Next scene, Skip, and Escape, with focus returning to the replay control after the film.
Reduced-motion cinematic artwork now redraws when you resize the window or rotate your phone. Repeated clicks no longer interrupt the opening film’s descent transition.
Device reduced-motion changes now update hub effects and motion controls immediately. Sound and motion switches have clearer screen-reader names.
Hero ability controls show recharge seconds and recovery time, with a ring that respects your upgraded cooldown. Auto Wave and Auto Gene clearly show HIVE while Hive Intelligence manages them.
★ Complete Campaign Stage 5 to unlock continuous Hive Intelligence in Campaign and Infinite, including new campaign stages.
Toggle the hive on to place towers, buy upgrades, merge organisms, start waves and choose recommended genes automatically.
Hive Intelligence directs your lead hero toward threats and uses their ability automatically, without buying the separate Auto-Cast upgrade.
Take control at any time with the ON/OFF toggle or draft Stop button. Pause suspends automation; each new run starts with Hive Intelligence off.
New guide and dev blog explain the stage-5 unlock, automatic actions and manual takeover.
★ New system: Class Bonds. Field 2, 4 or 6 towers and heroes of one class in a run and its bond wakes at tier I, II or III, for as long as they stay deployed

Six bonds with six jobs: Kinetic hits harder, Caustic hits harder and fires faster, Viral fires much faster, Neural fires faster and hits harder, Vital mends your Hive Core every wave, and Resonant speeds up every tower

★ The new Class Bonds screen (Evolution Hub, after Campaign Stage 13) lists every class and its members; spend Genome Cores to level a bond up and strengthen all three tiers in every run (up to ×1.8), raising your Power
The Run Build panel shows every class you've fielded and how close the next tier is, conveyor pods carry their class mark, and a waking bond is announced on the battlefield
Bonds are introduced with a card, a short guided tour and an in-fight field note, and each has its own Help entry
New dev blog post: “Class Bonds: build around a class, and make it stronger”; the Tower Guide covers bonds
Release notes 'Class Bonds' curated; site + PIL regenerated
★ New players are walked through their first trips back to base step by step: open the menus, buy a first upgrade, crack a first container and see what to do next, pressing every button yourself
While the guide runs, the Command Center shows only what it has introduced: the event banner, side panels and reward pop-ups wait, and the goal list shows your two nearest goals
★ Early Call: each called wave's gene draft now arrives the moment that wave's last enemy falls, so drafts no longer pile up three or four in a row
Best Move and the Command Center's suggestions no longer offer upgrades in systems you haven't unlocked (they could level Adaptations before the Adaptation Chamber opened)
Busy fights and tower clicks do less work per frame, with about a third less memory churn, and the battlefield looks exactly the same
New dev blog post: “Your first steps, walked with you”
★ The game starts sooner: what your browser downloads before the first screen went from about 667 KB to 549 KB (compressed), roughly a sixth less
Each screen now brings its own styling when you open it, and the full Help text and patch-note history load only when you open them
Help: the Towers, Heroes and Infinite entries show their related topics again
New dev blog post: “A lighter first download” — what we cut, and how we checked nothing looks different
★ In a phone’s web browser the game now fits what the address bar leaves visible — menus, Results and dialogs no longer slip under it
★ Android and iPad: your first tap goes full screen (Settings can turn it off), and ⛶ in the top bar brings it back
iPhone: a one-time card shows how to add the game to your Home Screen to play without the address bar; the installed game now opens in landscape
Upright phones keep a bigger battlefield during runs: the loot meter folds into a thin strip and the controls tighten
The top bar no longer runs off the edge on small phones held sideways
★ Your first hour, one beat at a time: each run now teaches at most two new systems in full (the first run used to list eleven at once); the rest wait their turn and are already in Help
★ Fight controls explain themselves the moment they matter: Early Call, game speed, the red defense line and hero evolution each get a one-line field note mid-fight, pointing at the control
Every new screen arrives with its guided tour, including the Tower Lab, Hero Hall and Infinite, which used to open with no introduction
★ Full sound pass: combat, reward and UI sounds rebuilt with more weight, effects now cut through the music, frequent sounds no longer repeat identically, and big moments get a little room
New Effects and Music volume sliders in Settings and the pause menu
Long sounds (the opening film's rumble, title and dive, boss stings) no longer cut off after half a second
Help no longer lists systems whose screens haven't opened yet
The opening film's title now follows your Motion setting
★ The opening film is rebuilt around a turn: a new scene where real towers burst out of the ground, the swarm breaks on the line and every kill streams home to your Hive Core
★ The swarm in the opening film is the game's own creatures, climbing out of the crust with a giant rising past the camera; the veins now take the whole steel frame
The title assembles letter by letter over the organism you have become, and DEFEND · EVOLVE · CONSUME lands one word at a time
Two new film sounds: towers bursting from the ground, and the swarm breaking on the line
The title no longer clips to "ASSIMILAT…" on narrow phones
The opening film loads only when it plays, so the game's first download is smaller

★ Every tower fires in its damage type — Kinetic darts, Caustic globs, Viral spores, Neural bolts, Vital orbs and Resonant pulses — in its own colour; hits, splash blasts and kills land in the striker’s colours, and mortar blasts show their real radius

★ Boss attacks telegraph on the battlefield: a ring shows where a heal, gun-silence or drag lands and a closing lock shows when; a core-shot visibly crawls toward your Hive Core, and bosses no longer white out under heavy fire
★ Mega cataclysms mark your Hive Core and strike down to it; weak points flinch and show the damage each volley takes
★ Every biome now looks like a place — frost-cracked slate, lava-seamed basalt, moss, mire, bone fields — with its own drifting air; obstacles are rock, not grids
★ Placing a tower lands with a thump, upgrades and strains molt the organism, maxed ones raise a column of light — and the Hive Core wears its health as an arc

★ Rarity looks the same everywhere: gear, gene cards, containers and cosmetics glow, shimmer and edge-light in their tier like draft cards; the Vault shows the rarity you actually pulled, and Genome Rank promotions get a golden ceremony
Hero abilities land with a clear lock-on and impact frame, and heroes breathe and recoil when they strike

★ The Hive reads your board: every tower is graded on reach, area damage, armour pierce, burst and control, and adapted waves probe what yours is thinnest against — the briefing names it (⌖ ARTILLERY · lacks burst)

★ Account Level keeps pace deep into the game: past Campaign Stage 30 your depth multiplies every run’s Account XP (DEPTH ×N on Results) — deep levels pay smaller, more frequent rewards; the weekly and monthly XP boards still count pure play time
Hive Intelligence spends overflowing Biomass on Splice — the extra draft it opens is still yours to pick
Busy fights read better: small damage numbers and repeated reaction callouts fade when the field is crowded, and slowed or disrupted enemies show a grip instead of another glowing ring
Goal estimates are honest for returning players (shown as “25+ runs” until the game has seen a few of your runs), and a stage within reach reads as an attempt or two
The battlefield floor no longer redraws itself every frame — the single biggest render cost is gone
A boss’s fired ability now stays on its banner long enough to read, and enemy spawn effects draw in their own colours
Opening a Bio-Container answers your tap instantly, and the Genome Rank promotion fits small phone screens
★ Your drafted gene cards no longer make the Hive adapt harder — a good pick now carries the run

★ The Hive probes your defense: from wave 4 on a frontier stage, a strong board meets the enemy role it covers least — fliers, artillery or burrowers — and the wave briefing names them before you launch
★ The Hive now reads your whole board — towers fielded included — and from wave 4 answers with faster, denser and tougher waves, so frontier stages bite again without dragging on
★ Readiness tells the truth: the under-powered warning (and the Farm Infinite suggestion) now appears only below 70% of a stage’s recommended Power — where runs are usually lost
After you call waves early, the back-to-back gene drafts say how many more are owed instead of repeating “wave cleared”
★ No more wave-1 coin flips: Campaign openings keep fliers out of wave 1, a stage’s Mega surfaces with wave 3, and your free first organism now answers the stage’s opening threats
★ The Hive adapts: from wave 4 and on every boss, Campaign waves rise to meet a snowballing board (the briefing shows ▲ ADAPTED ×N) — losses now come late in a run, where your choices matter
★ Call early: press ⏩ (or Space) mid-wave to launch the next wave now for bonus Biomass — every gene draft you skip is still dealt when the field clears
★ Gene drafts now deal cards for the towers and heroes that actually carry your run, and ◆ PICK marks the best fit — not the rarest card
★ Splice: when Biomass piles up between waves, spend it on an extra gene draft. Campaign runs from Stage 8 open with an Opening Draft
★ Goals tell the truth: every next milestone shows how many runs away it really is, and Home’s main button says Farm Infinite when a stage outweighs you
★ Gear keeps getting better: item level now rises with how deep you have pushed, with no cap — Rampant and Apex drops mean more, and T6 affixes appear deep in the Campaign
★ Mega stages no longer wall you for a day, and every organ you burst — even in a lost raid — advances your Mega Hunt rank for Genome Cores
★ Boss Rush has a real wall: bosses are sized to your Power and the next column won’t wait. Records restarted with it — your old best is kept as a Pre-wall Record and the leaderboard started fresh
Achievement ladders keep milestones coming at any depth, the daily Bio-Cache grows with your income, commons get Claim all in the Specimen Cabinet, and one tap rebuilds your Genome after a Molt
Nothing you earn un-earns itself: Gear Codex entries are permanent and a Molt never demotes your Genome Rank
Infinite now ends through attrition instead of one wipe — you see the end coming over several waves
Hive Intelligence builds your opening towers before it spends on hero stats
Defeats show your board size against what winning boards field, and when your first flier went down; the mission card shows wave 1
A Daily run that used the draft reroll no longer fails replay verification
The Mega bar no longer covers the gene draft’s header, and the Boss Rush tray no longer clips its last pod on wide screens
★ The last kill of every wave lands: time slows for a heartbeat, the camera leans in, and the wave-clear fanfare plays on the kill itself — deeper and longer when a boss or Mega falls
★ Victory feels like a takeover: the hive washes across the whole battlefield, and your summary opens over the board you just won. Defeats drain and crack the field from the breach point
★ On desktop the battlefield no longer ends at the board edge: the biome, its veins and the creeping infestation continue into the frame around it, and a Mega’s limbs reach in from beyond
★ Cutscenes move: the camera drifts and punches on the score’s beats, and every Mega premiere finally shows its monster — rising from silhouette, igniting its weak points, and falling
The last enemy’s death burst no longer freezes mid-air while the gene draft opens
Home’s Hive Intel feed and the Vault history no longer drop or double a row
The “Also earned” row on Results no longer trips over achievement pop-ups
On phones held sideways, the opening film keeps its captions off the Hive Core
★ New tower: Gristle Warren — a barracks whose thralls body-block the lane
★ New tower: Tick Battery — a long-range plague seeder that infects three hosts at once
★ New tower: Keening Quill — cracks armour for your whole board
★ New hero: the Myceliarch — a fungal gatekeeper who rots every leak at the Core, earned at 8,000 kills
★ Six puzzle enemies from Stage 4 — Chitin Scuttler, Blight Moth, Marrow Borer, Shellback Bombard, Veil Moth and Wisp Mother — each demanding the right answer
New achievements: The Answer Key, Every Question Answered and The Gate Holds
★ Boss kills land: a freeze-frame, a shockwave and a fall card — and centre-screen announcements no longer pile on top of each other
Damage numbers are bolder and readable over anything, and picking a gene card now has a real moment
New Motion settings (screen shake %, damage numbers, flashes) that respect your device’s reduced-motion setting
Every sound plays: Arena victory and defeat and the Maw’s shot had been silent, and a boss death has its own sound instead of the breach alarm
★ Won a Campaign stage? Results now offers the next stage directly
One “Claim all” on the Quest Board, Season Pass and Milestones — and the Season Pass clears a full backlog in one press
Phones held upright now show Results and the Boss Rush roulette instead of “turn your device”
★ Back steps back through menus and pauses a live run instead of quitting it; Escape closes pop-ups
Advice like “Farm Infinite” is one tap away (Go ▸)
Hub badges count decisions instead of piling up to “9+”, and Continue Campaign is always on screen
Screens open without a loading flash, and a screen that fails to load can be retried instead of breaking the game
Every screen has one name everywhere — the Specimen Vault is now the Specimen Cabinet
Long screens (Hero Hall, Evolution HQ, Gene Archive) get jump chips and folding sections, and a loadout strip sits beside every launch
Tap any currency in the top bar to learn what it is; small text is easier to read
Every Gene Card level now visibly raises your Power, even small economy upgrades like Engorged Reactor
Strain Samples no longer pile up deep in the game: once a strain has banked every Sample its remaining stars could cost, extra Samples from Bio-Containers become Gene Essence
A Mitotic Horror falls once — its split pieces no longer each announce a kill
Watching a replay no longer adds its kills to your own Bestiary, Mega records or nemesis revenge
Replay links recorded before an update play again instead of showing an error, and the replay theater shows boss falls
The Bio-Dex counts only real Brood Tyrants
Field Guides open folded sections while they run
The Screen shake slider (and every slider) is a comfortable touch target on phones and tablets
The website catches up: new devlog “Feel and Flow”, refreshed features, screenshots and trailer

★ Molting no longer wipes your whole Genome engine: from your second Molt on, every upgrade keeps a growing share of its levels (+1.25% per Molt, up to 70%), so Power dips instead of crashing — and the Molt Chamber shows your Power after the Molt before you confirm
Upgrades that promise an effect around the victim (Acid Lancet, Basilisk, Chrysalis, Siphon, Coil, Spire, Spitfang) now land on the struck enemy instead of around the tower
Miasma Lung’s infection-spread upgrades work: an infection now spreads by the reach of the tower that laid it
“Stage N+1 ▸” on Results lets you pick the next stage’s boon instead of taking the default
Fixed a crash that could end a run when a boss died on a slow frame (most often on phones)
Rank promotions, level-ups and other pop-ups now wait until your Arena match is over instead of covering the field
★ New system: Threat Ladder
★ New system: Arena Layouts
★ New achievement: The Apex Horde Falls
★ New achievement: Into the Red
★ New achievement: Raised the Stakes
Campaign Stages 1–3 now rise in difficulty instead of trivial, trivial, wall
New screens unlock gradually over your first ~10 hours instead of all at once
Fewer currencies early (secondary wallets group as Materials), chore rewards auto-claim into Results, and badges only where there's a decision
Five side screens became tabs inside their host screens (31 → 26 menu destinations)
Flanking and pincer layouts wait until Campaign Stage 11
Field Guide Skip works again; Champion Contracts and Boss Rush previews only appear once they're open
Phones: the Hive key shows a lock when it's off, and the Help chip is easier to tap
The Home command strip no longer shows stats for screens you haven't opened yet
Belgium and the Netherlands: nothing that can end in a randomized reward is sold for money (loot-box law) — everything stays earnable in play
Website refresh to the current game + a standing freshness rule
One graduation reward at the end of onboarding — the HUD tour no longer pays a second, identical card
The combat tutorial follows a real run: callouts stay off the lane, the draft cards and your ability, and the HUD shows a truthful 2-wave count
After a run: one unlock summary instead of a stack of popups; achievement toasts wait their turn and collapse
Advice never points at a locked screen, and no "Under-Powered" warning right after a flawless clear
Defeat debrief on Results — how close you were, what got through, one tip — and the real name of the boss you slew
A bigger board on every screen, plus dedicated portrait and landscape phone layouts for runs
13 arena layouts — Campaign, Daily and Infinite now vary the battlefield
Rule Genes: 25 build-defining gene cards, and every draft guarantees one rule-changing card once you've earned one
Hive Intelligence and Auto Gene now run only on content you've already cleared
Fixed hero max HP dropping after a Vitality upgrade; the readout never shows HP above max
Commissioning offers one clear guest choice
Faster first load: screens load on demand, and the game works offline after your first visit
Paid random containers can be switched off per region (Belgium and the Netherlands by default)
The ASSIMILATION wordmark fits on phones
Guided Unlocks: full-curve coverage — every taught wing walks you through itself
Hive Intelligence: universal in-run best-upgrade executive + calendar test fixes
★ New system: Hive Intelligence (in-run)
Living battlefield: organism anticipation, idle life, and reactivity
Mega-boss stall fix, self-sealing patch notes, lab adaptation links
Boss Rush free-entry badge: volatile daily notification watermarks
Mega bosses: raid hit audio + waves hold for the kill outside campaign
Mega fight-timeline probe + organ drought valve: rebuild verdict grounded in numbers
Mega dormancy: the organism burrows between waves, the raid bar greys out
Mega dormancy identity layer: seven sleeping silhouettes over the burrow mound

★ New system: Reward Loop Architecture
★ New system: Player Telemetry & Analytics

★ New tower: Basilisk Maw

★ New system: Online Foundation

★ New achievement: Baseline Genome
★ New achievement: Apex Strand
★ New achievement: Ancestral Strand
★ New achievement: Serial Mutator
★ New achievement: The Helix Reforms
